raw_response:
I farm the way I have always farmed: I start from what I did last year, then I look at the sky, the water in the well, and what the people around me are doing. On my 5 mu, I will still do wheat and then maize on the same land. I do not like taking chances with grain. If I save too much on fertilizer and the ears come out short, that loss is bigger than wasting a little fertilizer money. So I will keep the land in grain, use the kinds most people around here plant, and feed the wheat a bit heavier with phosphate and the maize a bit heavier with potash. With well water in hand, I will not wait for the sky if the field turns dry. For wheat, I will use improved seed, rotary till after the maize stubble is handled, put the base fertilizer down first, then topdress once when the wheat stands up in spring. I will water about 3 times if the year is normal. For maize, I will sow right after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed, rotary once to catch the season fast, put fertilizer under or beside the row, and chase one more nitrogen feeding later. I will spray only when needed, but I will not let weeds and worms get ahead of me. On 5 mu, every bag costs money, so I will keep the plan steady and practical, not fancy.
